column1: # AUTHORED. The seed sources for the CDS database, their role, and why each is here.
# Never generated. holobase source_ids are from _refdata/holobase.db `source`.
# role=secondary  corrects a known blind spot in the primary
# role=host       the plant sink, so host reads have a correct home instead of being
#                 absorbed by the nearest fungal CDS and reported as fungal
# role=dropped    was the scope basis for db_v3 and is no longer

column6: 20204 on plants; 1488 with a scaffold+ assembly
column7: 827,645 records. recorded_on, NOT pathogenicity, which is exactly why it reaches the saprotrophs, endophytes and epiphytes that PHI-base structurally cannot. CC0.

USDA is a herbarium records database, so leaf yeasts are barely recorded as "fungus on host X": Papiliotrema, Dioszegia, Cystofilobasidium and Udeniomyces appear at 1-2 records each, and Candida and Mrakia not at all. But abundance data says 7 of the top 20 wheat genera ARE yeasts. USDA alone would miss that layer. See residents.tsv.
What exists to build from. holobase's is_annotated is 1 on EVERY row, so it cannot filter for annotation; annotation comes from NCBI at selection time.
The 4 cohort crops plus 2 outgroups. See hosts.tsv.

db_v3's seed basis, via 01_stat. DROPPED 2026-10-13: 01_stat is out of the pipeline, and PHI-base resolves to only 340 fungi because `pathogenic` excludes every non-pathogen. Keeping it as the scope basis would reproduce the gap this redesign exists to close. It remains REFERENCE DATA (phibase_db.json still labels which taxa are declared pathogens, used by 05_filter), just not the scope.
